advice: Test a bounded 64-column output-row panel using a separately prepared, byte-audited LIBXSMM helper for M=512,N=64,K=512, beta zero, and leading dimensions 512. In gemm, replace the n=512 full-kernel call with eight helper calls for row bands r=0,64,...,448; set parameters[4]=B, parameters[10]=A+r*512, and parameters[16]=C+r*512, with all other fields zero. This is a distinct panel width from the measured 32-row helper and one-entry wrapper. The hypothesis is that wider panels reduce call and SME transition overhead relative to sixteen calls; the tradeoff is larger per-call scratch and packing. Keep allocation and all work inside the timed call. Preserve the full512 kernel and the general-size fallback. If the exact helper is unavailable or fails byte and ABI validation, abstain rather than synthesize a new generated shape.
risks: The 64-row helper is not supplied, so this experiment is not currently implementable by a tool-limited agent. Its generated shape, ABI mapping, scratch bounds, and full-GEMM correctness need host-side validation first. Fewer calls do not establish a gain; the larger packed panel may offset reduced entry overhead. Do not attribute any result to call count alone.
